chapter_seo_title: The School: Li Huowang Uses a Bank Robbery as Proof of a Hallucination
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang reaches Yang Na’s school, ready to break the illusion by any means necessary. When a bank robbery erupts, he sees it as proof the world is fake. A chilling chapter of self-destructive resolve.
og_title: Li Huowang Hunts for Yang Na in a Hostage Crisis
og_description: “Could it get any faker than this?” Li Huowang uses a coincidental bank robbery as final proof this world is a hallucination, preparing for a brutal self-sacrifice.
twitter_title: The Ultimate Proof of a Fake World: A Bank Robbery
twitter_description: Li Huowang finds the absurdity of a hostage crisis *hilarious*—it’s the final validation he needs to act in a “hallucinatory” world. A chilling read.

lore_anchors.definition: In the novel, the boundary between real and fake is constantly contested; events like bank robberies become “too contrived” for the protagonist to accept as real.
A real-world crime scenario that Li Huowang interprets as “narrative convenience,” a common logical flaw in a fabricated reality.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang trust the bank robbery?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He sees the extreme coincidence as a failure of the hallucination’s logic—it’s *too* convenient, which means it’s fake.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What are Li Huowang's instructions to Bai Lingmiao and Li Sui?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is pre-authorizing a self-sacrifice ritual from the *Thousand Greats Record*, telling them to inflict the ultimate pain on him so he can “wake up.”
